findings.title: Overview of rural and small towns water services in Northern Region
findings.summary: The 2014 service monitoring round assessed rural and small towns water services in Northern Region of Ghana.

findings.title: Aquifer storage and recharge suitability in northern Ghana
findings.summary: Most of the study area has static water levels from 10 to 70 m, suitable for aquifer storage and recharge techniques.

findings.title: Flood impacts on water quality in Tamale
findings.summary: Floods deteriorate water quality of unprotected sources in Tamale, increasing faecal contamination risks.

findings.title: Tamale-Damongo Water Supply Project financing and progress
findings.summary: Ghana Water Limited is advancing the €312 million Tamale-Damongo Water Supply Project with EU and other partners' funding.

findings.title: Access to improved drinking-water in Ghana
findings.summary: Urban population access to improved drinking water increased from 73% in 2016 to 83% in 2018 in Ghana.

findings.title: Basement aquifers characteristics in Ghana
findings.summary: Basement aquifers have transmissivity between 0.2 and 119 m²/day and borehole depths from 40 to 200 m.

findings.title: Flood hazards in Northern Ghana including Tamale
findings.summary: Northern Region is among the most flood-prone areas in Ghana, with floods causing significant national impacts.

findings.title: Tamale water system project plans
findings.summary: Plans include building a pumping station at Yapei to produce about 30 million gallons of water for Tamale Metropolis.

findings.title: Water service level standards in Ghana
findings.summary: Water service standards include a maximum distance of 500 metres to the farthest household for rural water schemes.

findings.title: Groundwater aquifers in northern Ghana
findings.summary: Aquifers in northern Ghana are semi-confined with depths ranging from 10 to 60 m, recharged mainly by precipitation.

findings.title: Local climate change impacts in Tamale
findings.summary: Tamale residents report floods (48%), increasing temperatures (15%), and erratic rainfall (13.8%) as climate change impacts.

findings.title: Government plans for Tamale water project construction
findings.summary: Government budgeted for a pumping station on the White Volta at Yapei to supply additional water to Tamale.

findings.title: Household water sources and storage in Northern Ghana
findings.summary: Over half the population depend on surface water sources often contaminated with faecal matter in Northern Ghana.

findings.title: Groundwater availability for irrigation in northeast Ghana
findings.summary: Groundwater levels are usually shallow, making it relatively easy to abstract water by hand digging shallow wells.

findings.title: Research on local adaptation to climate change in Tamale
findings.summary: Studies document grassroots coping strategies for climate change impacts in Tamale, Northern Ghana.

findings.title: Government to locally fund Tamale water project after funding delay
findings.summary: Government will mobilize local funds to execute the Tamale water supply project after €277 million facility delay.
